title: Relay canonical intake envelope, version 1
description: The structural half of the intake contract. Rules that relate two members to each other — timestamp ordering, identity derivation, digest length against its named algorithm, size ceilings — cannot be expressed in JSON Schema and are stated normatively in docs/intake-envelope.md. A document accepted here is well-shaped, not necessarily conforming; run the reference validator for the full contract.

envelope_version.description: Major version of the contract. Only the major appears on the wire; a consumer must never branch on a minor version, because a change it would need to branch on is by definition breaking.

intake_id.description: Identity of the captured item, derived from source.system and source.external_id. Stable across revisions of the same item.

kind.description: What was captured. A consumer routes on this, so the vocabulary is closed; x- names an experimental kind that must not be routed structurally.

occurred_at.description: When the captured thing happened. Absent when the source cannot say.

captured_at.description: When the source system recorded the item.

system.description: Vendor-neutral identifier for the capture system. Part of the identity derivation, so it must be stable for the lifetime of the deployment.

external_id.description: The item's identifier within that system. Opaque to Relay.

external_revision.description: Optional source-side revision marker. Advisory: content.digest is what actually distinguishes revisions.

provenance.description: How this envelope came to exist. Excluded from the item projection, so re-emission may change it freely.

acquired_at.description: When the adapter read the item from the source.

emitted_at.description: When the adapter produced this envelope.

run_id.description: Optional collection-run identifier, for operational correlation only.

content.description: Identity of the preserved bytes. Distinguishes one revision of an item from another.

byte_length.description: Length of the preserved payload in bytes.

payload.description: Where the preserved bytes are, and when they were preserved. A reference, never the bytes themselves.

uri.description: Absolute URI resolvable by the operator's storage. Schemes that inline data are forbidden by the normative rules; JSON Schema states the shape only.

preserved_at.description: When the adapter durably wrote the payload. Precedes provenance.emitted_at: an envelope must not reference bytes that did not yet exist.

metadata.description: Source-neutral facts about the item, sufficient for structural routing and insufficient to reconstruct the content. Vendor-specific attributes belong in the preserved payload, not here.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 instant with a literal Z offset. Only Z is admitted: an offset-bearing timestamp denotes the same instant and renders differently, which would make canonical form ambiguous.
